hook: 5 minutes is all it takes to check for oral cancer at home
caption: Most people don't know that oral cancer can show up as something as simple as a sore that won't heal or a patch of white or red tissue inside your mouth. A quick self-exam once a month can help you catch changes early, when they're most treatable. Start by looking at your lips, gums, the roof and floor of your mouth, and both sides of your tongue. You're looking for anything that feels like a lump, looks unusual, or has been there for more than two weeks. Difficulty swallowing that's new or persistent is worth noting too. None of this requires any tools or training, just a mirror and a couple of minutes. If something looks or feels off, that's not a reason to panic. It's a reason to get it checked. Start your free risk screening at oralcheck.org.
